messages:
jamie: Heads-up — canary rollout for inference-service v2.3 showing a spike in 5xxs from the canary pool since 09:12 UTC. Pager fired but when I tried to open the canary metrics dashboard it returned 404. Anyone seeing the same?

oncall-bot: incident created INC-2026-021 — Pager: #eng-oncall · Severity: P2 · assigned to oncall rotation. Link: https://incidents.redwood.local/INC-2026-021 :rotating_light:

maria: I'm on it. Which region is the canary in?

jamie: eu-west1-gpu-a — traffic split ~0.7%. Initial errors: gateway 500s, some kv-cache errors in logs.

kevin: I can see p50->p99 latency drift for text-gen routes on the canary; also alert spam — the canary alert is firing per-pod which is creating noisy duplicates.

oliver: Confirm the dashboard 404. The grafana panel id used by the deploy is different from the one in current dashboards. Looks like the monitoring-migration PR for dashboard mappings didn't land. Queries are returning 404 -> alerts fallback to firing on default thresholds.

jamie: That's bad — need quick mitigation. Any customer-facing errors reported?

kevin: From logs (sample):
```
2026-03-15T09:13:02Z gateway[gw-12]: ERR 500 "kv-cache-miss" route=text-gen user=svc-frontend trace=abcd1234
2026-03-15T09:13:05Z canary-eu-1 pod[5]: WARN attach-kv: missing-kv-segment id=0x7f
2026-03-15T09:14:10Z gateway[gw-12]: ERR 500 "model-timeout" latency_ms=2100
```
No high-sev customer tickets in Zendesk yet but we should assume degraded latency for canary traffic.

maria: Mitigation plan: 1) pause the rollout, 2) flip feature-flag kill-switch to route canary traffic back to stable variant, 3) mute noisy alert group while we verify rollback. I'll start.

maria: /release pause rollout inference-service v2.3 --scope=canary

oliver: Observed that the feature flag key for canary routing was renamed in the release. If we flip the old key it won't affect pods. Need to flip via feature-flag service with the new key name.

maria: Doing the kill-switch now — updating FF key `routes.inference.canary.v2.enabled=false` via ff-admin console.

deploy-bot: Rollback initiated by maria at 09:18 UTC for inference-service v2.3 (canary subset). Rolling back 12 pods. Progress: 12/12 -> success. :white_check_mark:

jamie: Nice. Maria — can you own verification and the handoff? I'll be leaving the oncall window in 20m.

maria: I'll own verification. Kevin can you mute the duplicate alert noise? It's flooding the channel and making triage hard.

kevin: Muting alert rule group `canary-5xx-flood` for 30m (annotation: "muted during rollback verification"). Also added a temporary suppression to avoid multiple pages for the same incident.

oliver: Root cause (quick): monitoring migration renamed metric namespaces and dashboard IDs. The deploy updated alerting to reference the new metrics but the dashboard lookup table didn't sync, so grafana panel queries returned 404 and some alert queries fell back to a boolean that evaluated true in absence of data -> noisy alerts and SLO confusion.

jamie: Customer impact summary for support: ~0.5% of traffic hit the canary; observed increased latency and a small spike in 500s for long-prompt requests. No major customer outages reported. Please tell support to monitor for any delayed tickets.

maria: Support notified — creating a short blurb for status page: "Minor latency and errors observed for a subset of users during a canary rollout; rollback completed and services are stable."

kevin: Follow-ups I'm doing: 1) unmute alerts after verification complete, 2) create a hotfix to make alert queries resilient to missing metrics (use exists(...) guard), 3) add an alert dedupe rule to prevent per-pod fanout.

oliver: I'll fix the dashboard mapping table and open a PR to ensure dashboard IDs are part of the release validation. Adding a CI check: validate_grafana_links.sh will run post-publish.

maria: Owner assignment for postmortem: dashboard fix -> oliver, alert rule resiliency -> kevin, CI dashboard check -> jamie. I'll start the incident doc in #postmortems and add these owners.

oncall-bot: Handoff scheduled: jamie -> maria (09:20–17:00 UTC).

maria: Verification done: traffic back to stable, 5xxs returned to baseline, SLO burn stopped. Will keep monitoring for 30m.

oncall-bot: incident INC-2026-021 closed by maria at 09:35 UTC. Duration ~23m.

jamie: Quick retrospective notes: 1) ensure monitoring migrations have consumer-safe fallback, 2) add a small synthetic check in release pipeline to open the canary dashboard URL, 3) improve FF key naming docs to avoid silent mismatches.

maria: Adding those to the RCA doc now. Thanks all for quick action. :thumbsup:
